post.description:
Run a search against a configured search tool.

The tool is taken from ``search_tool_name``, which may be omitted when the
deployment's ``web_search_default_tool`` names one, or when exactly one
tool is configured. Such a call runs on the workspace's organization search
key when it has one.

Authentication modes:
- Master key: the ``user`` field is required and may name any existing user.
- API key: usage and spend bind to the key's own user. A ``user`` field
  naming a different user is rejected with 403 (or ignored, when the key's
  own ``reject_user_mismatch`` is false, or the deployment-wide setting is
  disabled and the key does not override it); it is never billed to that
  user.
- Service key: a ``user`` field names one of the key owner's end users,
  created on first use on the budget ``Otari-End-User-Budget`` names (or
  the key's default), and is billed and rate limited as that end user, as
  on chat completions.

Fetch one page through a configured fetch tool.

The tool is taken from ``fetch_tool_name``, which may be omitted: the
deployment's ``web_fetch_default_tool`` then serves, else ``builtin_fetch``,
the gateway's own fetcher. Such a call runs on the workspace's organization
fetch key when it has one. While the deployment's ``web_fetch_enabled`` is
off, the call is refused, as ``otari_web_fetch`` is. The URL must pass the
workspace's domain lists and the gateway's own checks: a public http or
https URL that names no private address. The built-in fetcher also checks
where each host resolves.

Authentication modes:
- Master key: the ``user`` field is required and may name any existing user.
- API key: usage and spend bind to the key's own user. A ``user`` field
  naming a different user is rejected with 403 (or ignored, when the key's
  own ``reject_user_mismatch`` is false, or the deployment-wide setting is
  disabled and the key does not override it); it is never billed to that
  user.
- Service key: a ``user`` field names one of the key owner's end users,
  created on first use on the budget ``Otari-End-User-Budget`` names (or
  the key's default), and is billed and rate limited as that end user, as
  on chat completions.

Run code in the gateway's sandbox and return its output.

The run is admitted as an ``otari_code_execution`` call is: a workspace whose
code execution policy is off is refused, and its execution ceiling and pinned
image apply. It is priced under ``otari:code_execution`` and reserved against
the caller's budgets. ``file_ids`` puts uploads in the working directory, and
each file the code writes comes back with a ``file_id``. ``container: "auto"``
holds the sandbox after the run and names it in ``Otari-Container-Id``;
sending that id back runs in the same sandbox, with its files and
interpreter state.

Authentication modes:
- Master key: the ``user`` field is required and may name any existing user.
- API key: usage and spend bind to the key's own user. A ``user`` field
  naming a different user is rejected with 403 (or ignored, when the key's
  own ``reject_user_mismatch`` is false, or the deployment-wide setting is
  disabled and the key does not override it); it is never billed to that
  user.
- Service key: a ``user`` field names one of the key owner's end users,
  created on first use on the budget ``Otari-End-User-Budget`` names (or
  the key's default), and is billed and rate limited as that end user.

get.description:
List the tools Otari runs itself, with the declaration forms it accepts.

Called with an API key, a tool its workspace does not allow is listed as
unavailable. Every other `tools[]` entry, including provider-native keywords
not listed here, is forwarded to the upstream provider untouched.

What the calling key may still spend, and every cap that decides it.

Lists the budget the key's user is on and each spend ceiling on a scope the
key bills to (the key itself, its user's memberships, its workspace and its
organization), as the budget gate counts them: recorded use plus the holds of
requests in flight. A period that has ended reads as the fresh one the next
request starts. ``remaining_usd`` is the least any cap on every provider
leaves, which is what a request can still spend before a 403. Caps shared with
the rest of the workspace or organization report only what they leave.

List the end users of the calling service key, oldest first.

Requires a service key. End users belong to the key's user, so every service key of one user lists the same
end users. A deleted end user is not listed. ``external_id`` reads one end user by any id, one containing '/'
included, as a list of zero or one.

delete.description:
Delete one end user of the calling service key, or a page of those created before a time.

Requires a service key, and exactly one of ``external_id`` and ``created_before``. ``external_id`` deletes that
end user, any id, one containing '/' included, and answers 404 when it has none. ``created_before`` deletes up
to ``limit`` of the oldest end users created before then; call again until ``deleted`` is 0. An end user's
telemetry and agent traces are erased with it. The end user's row and spend are kept: a request naming it again
revives it with what it had spent, so deleting one cannot clear its budget. A deleted end user is neither listed
nor counted.

parameters.name: limit

schema.description: The most end users one call deletes with `created_before`.

get.description:
List the budgets the calling service key may put its end users on, with their limits and end user counts.

Requires a service key. Each budget's name, limits and period are the ones every end user on it is held to. The
counts cover the end users of the key's user, blocked ones included and deleted ones not.

Look up a request's settled cost by the ``Otari-Request-ID`` it was sent.

This is how a caller recovers the cost of a request whose response never
carried one: a stream that failed or was disconnected mid-response, or a
request that errored. An API key sees only the requests it made; the master
key sees any. Returns 404 until the request has settled (its rows are written
by a background writer, so a lookup made the instant a stream closes can
precede them), and for an id that is unknown or belongs to another key, with
no way to tell those apart. A stream that failed, including one the provider
cut, always writes an error row. A stream the client abandoned before the
provider reported usage, with no gateway tool work, writes a row only under
the ``estimate`` policy, billed on an estimate; otherwise it writes none, so
its id stays 404.

code.title: Code
code.description: Python source to run in the sandbox

container.title: Container
container.description: 'auto' to hold the sandbox after the run, or a container id an earlier response named in Otari-Container-Id to run in that sandbox again, with its files and interpreter state. Omitted, the sandbox is released when the run ends.

timeout_seconds.title: Timeout Seconds
timeout_seconds.description: How long the code may run. Never more than the workspace's code execution ceiling, or 60 seconds when it sets none.

file_ids.title: File Ids
file_ids.description: Uploads from POST /api/v1/files to put in the working directory before the code runs, each under its own filename.

CodeExecuteRequest.title: CodeExecuteRequest
CodeExecuteRequest.description: A direct code execution request: the code to run, and the sandbox to run it in.

return_code.title: Return Code
return_code.description: The program's exit status; null when the sandbox did not report one.

files.title: Files
files.description: The files the code wrote. Empty when it wrote none, or where the Files API is off.

CodeExecuteResponse.title: CodeExecuteResponse
CodeExecuteResponse.description: A completed code execution. Code that failed is a completed execution with a nonzero ``return_code``.

filename.title: Filename
filename.description: The name the code gave it in the working directory

CodeExecutionOutputFile.title: CodeExecutionOutputFile
CodeExecutionOutputFile.description: A file the code wrote, stored in the Files API.

max_budget.title: Max Budget
max_budget.description: Dollars each end user may spend over the period

is_default.title: Is Default

end_user_count.title: End User Count
end_user_count.description: End users of the key's user on this budget, blocked ones included

EndUserBudgetPublic.title: EndUserBudgetPublic
EndUserBudgetPublic.description: A budget a service key may put its end users on, and how many of them are on it.

EndUserPublic.title: EndUserPublic
EndUserPublic.description: An end user of a service key, addressed by the id the service named it by.

budget_id.title: Budget Id
budget_id.description: A budget on the key's end_user_budget_ids

EndUserPut.title: EndUserPut
EndUserPut.description: Create an end user ahead of its first request, or move one, onto a budget on the key's list.

blocked.title: Blocked
blocked.description: Whether the end user is refused

budget_id.title: Budget Id
budget_id.description: A budget on the key's end_user_budget_ids to move the end user to

EndUserUpdate.title: EndUserUpdate
EndUserUpdate.description: Block, unblock or move an end user. An omitted field is left as it is.

deleted.title: Deleted
deleted.description: End users deleted by this call. A page as full as the limit may leave more.

EndUsersDeleted.title: EndUsersDeleted
EndUsersDeleted.description: How many end users a delete removed.

url.title: Url
url.description: The page to fetch: one public http or https URL.

fetch_tool_name.title: Fetch Tool Name
fetch_tool_name.description: Configured fetch tool to run on, builtin_fetch included. Optional: the deployment's web_fetch_default_tool serves, else builtin_fetch. Ignored on POST /api/v1/fetch/{fetch_tool_name}.

max_chars.title: Max Chars
max_chars.description: Cut the page text to this many characters. Unset, the tool's own max_chars option applies, else the provider's own limits.

include_raw.title: Include Raw
include_raw.description: Also return the provider's whole response, as raw. builtin_fetch calls no provider, so its raw holds only content_kind and redirect_count.

provider_options.title: Provider Options
provider_options.description: Native options for the provider that serves the call, under the provider's own names, as GET /api/v1/search-tools/providers?kind=fetch lists them. An option the provider does not take from a request is refused with a 400. On a call that names no tool they go to whichever provider serves it, so name the tool when they are meant for one provider.

FetchRequest.title: FetchRequest
FetchRequest.description: A direct fetch request: one page, read through the deployment's fetch tool or the one named.

fetch_tool.title: Fetch Tool
fetch_tool.description: The configured fetch tool that served the request

url.title: Url
url.description: The URL fetched, as asked, in canonical form.

final_url.title: Final Url
final_url.description: Where the page was found after redirects. The URL asked for when the provider does not report where a redirect led (reports_final_url in the provider catalog).

title.title: Title
title.description: The page's title; empty when the provider gave none.

content_type.title: Content Type
content_type.description: The page's content type; empty when the provider does not report one.

text.title: Text
text.description: The page's text, as the provider extracted it.

published.title: Published
published.description: When the page was published, where the provider reports it.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: Whether text is less than the whole page: the body or the extracted text hit a limit of the provider's, or max_chars cut it.

raw.title: Raw
raw.description: The provider's whole response, untouched; only when the request set include_raw.

FetchResponse.title: FetchResponse
FetchResponse.description: A completed direct fetch: one page's text and where it came from.

code.title: Code
code.description: Stable error code, also sent as the Otari-Error-Code header.

budgets_enforced.title: Budgets Enforced
budgets_enforced.description: False when budgets are off for this key: it is budget-exempt, or the deployment runs with budget_strategy disabled. True otherwise, even when no cap applies

remaining_usd.title: Remaining Usd
remaining_usd.description: The fewest dollars any dollar cap on every provider leaves; null when none applies. A token, request or provider-narrowed cap in limits can refuse a request sooner

limits.title: Limits
limits.description: The key's user's budget first, then each spend ceiling, the most specific first

KeyBudgetPublic.title: KeyBudgetPublic
KeyBudgetPublic.description: What the calling key may still spend, and every cap that decides it.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Where the cap sits: 'user' for the budget the key's user is on, or the scope of a spend ceiling: 'api_token', 'workspace_member', 'org_member', 'workspace' or 'organization'

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: The provider this cap is narrowed to, or null when it caps every one

resets_at.title: Resets At
resets_at.description: When the period ends and use starts again from zero; null for a cap that never resets

limit_usd.title: Limit Usd
limit_usd.description: Dollars allowed per period; null when uncapped or shared

used_usd.title: Used Usd
used_usd.description: Dollars spent and held this period; null when uncapped or shared

remaining_usd.title: Remaining Usd
remaining_usd.description: Dollars left this period; null when dollars are uncapped

KeyLimitPublic.title: KeyLimitPublic
KeyLimitPublic.description:
One cap a request made with the calling key has to pass.

``used_*`` counts what the budget gate counts: recorded use plus the holds of
requests still in flight. On a cap the key shares with the rest of its
workspace or organization the limit and the use are left out, and only what
is left is reported; that still moves as the others spend.

id.title: Id
id.description: The canonical tool type to put in `tools[]`.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the tool does, as the model is told.

available.title: Available
available.description: Whether a request from this caller may declare the tool: the deployment has enabled and configured it and, for an API key, the key's workspace allows it. A master key or a dashboard session gets the deployment's answer alone. A request declaring an unavailable tool is refused.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the tool is unavailable, `null` when it is available. `not_configured`: nothing is set up to run it (for web search, neither the deployment nor the API key's organization has a search provider). `workspace_disabled`: the API key's workspace does not allow it, which a workspace admin changes under Tools in the dashboard.

accepted_types.title: Accepted Types
accepted_types.description: Every `tools[].type` this deployment currently routes to the tool. Always includes the canonical `otari_*` type; for web search it also includes the provider-named keywords when interception is enabled and the deployment has a search of its own, and for code execution the provider-named keywords unless the deployment's executor is `provider`.

input_schema.title: Input Schema
input_schema.description: JSON Schema for the arguments the model supplies, as the model sees it.

ManagedTool.title: ManagedTool
ManagedTool.description: One tool the gateway can run itself.

RequestSettlement.title: RequestSettlement
RequestSettlement.description:
What one request settled at, summed over every usage row it wrote.

A routed request writes a row per attempt and a vision-normalized one a row for
the describe call, all sharing the ``Otari-Request-ID`` the caller was sent as
their ``request_group_id``, so this is the request's whole bill rather than one
attempt's. ``cost_usd`` uses the inline ``usage.cost_usd`` format and is null
when no row was priced.

search_tool_name.title: Search Tool Name
search_tool_name.description: Configured search tool to run against. Optional when the deployment names a default (web_search_default_tool) or has exactly one tool, and ignored on POST /api/v1/search/{search_tool_name}.

max_results.title: Max Results
max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return; 10 when unset. Lowered to the workspace's ceiling when it sets one, and to the provider's own maximum.

search_domain_filter.title: Search Domain Filter
search_domain_filter.description: Restrict results to these domains; prefix a domain with '-' to exclude it instead

country.title: Country
country.description: Two-letter ISO country code to localize results to

max_tokens_per_page.title: Max Tokens Per Page
max_tokens_per_page.description: Approximate cap on the page content returned per result

include_raw.title: Include Raw
include_raw.description: Also return the provider's whole response, as raw.

provider_options.title: Provider Options
provider_options.description: Native options for the provider that serves the call, under the provider's own names, as GET /api/v1/search-tools/providers lists them. An option the provider does not take from a request is refused with a 400. On a call that names no tool they go to whichever provider serves it, so name the tool when they are meant for one provider.

SearchRequest.title: SearchRequest
SearchRequest.description: A direct search request: LiteLLM's ``/v1/search`` body, plus ``include_raw`` and ``provider_options``.

search_tool.title: Search Tool
search_tool.description: The configured search tool that served the request

raw.title: Raw

title.description: The page's title; empty when the provider gave none.

snippet.title: Snippet
snippet.description: The page text the provider returned, else its excerpt, cut to the page budget.

last_updated.title: Last Updated
